title.en: Lesson 1. Before and After: -기 전에 & -(으)ㄴ 후에

blocks.md:
Two essential time chunks for sequencing events:

1. **[Verb Stem] + -기 전에** = Before doing...
2. **[Verb Stem-(으)ㄴ] + 후에** = After doing...

밥 먹**기 전에** 손을 씻어요. / Before eating, I wash my hands.
밥 먹**은 후에** 커피를 마셔요. / After eating, I drink coffee.

blocks.q: “밥 먹___ 전에 손을 씻어요.” Which ending fits “before”?
blocks.why: “Before doing” is always **-기 전에** → 먹기 전에. 먹은 후에 is “after doing”.

blocks.meaning: Let’s eat after the movie ends.
blocks.why: 끝나다 has no final 받침 on 나, so it takes -ㄴ 후에 → **끝난 후에**.

blocks.meaning: Before coming to Korea, I learned Korean.

blocks.hint: Before doing is always -기 전에, not -(으)ㄴ 전에.

blocks.q: Write it yourself: **“Let’s meet after class finishes.”**  (class = 수업, to finish = 끝나다)
blocks.hint: Use 끝난 후에 for “after it finishes”, and 만나요 for “let’s meet”.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “After eating, I drink coffee.”

blocks.md:
**-(으)ㄹ 때** means **when** or **at the time that**.

- No 받침 → **-ㄹ 때**: 가다 → **갈 때** (when going)
- Has 받침 → **-을 때**: 먹다 → **먹을 때** (when eating)
- Stem ends in ㄹ: 살다 → **살 때** (when living)

시간 **있을 때** 뭐 해요? / What do you do when you have time?

items.tip: I bought a gift when I went to Korea.
What do you do when you have time?
When I’m bored, I listen to music.

blocks.q: “시간이 있___ 때 전화하세요.” Which one attaches to 있다?
blocks.why: 있다 has a 받침 (ㅆ), so it takes **-을 때** → 있을 때.

blocks.meaning: When I am tired, I drink warm tea.
blocks.why: 피곤하다 ends in vowel 하, so it takes -ㄹ 때 → **피곤할 때**.

blocks.meaning: When I was young, I lived in Korea.
blocks.why: 어렸 has a 받침 (ㅆ), so it takes -을 때 → **어렸을 때** (when I was young).

blocks.q: Translate into Korean: **“What do you do when you have time?”**  (time = 시간, to have = 있다, what = 뭐, to do = 하다)
blocks.hint: Combine 시간(이) with 있다 + -(으)ㄹ 때, followed by 뭐 해요?
blocks.why: 시간(이) 있을 때 뭐 해요? 있다 takes -을 때.

blocks.q: Say it out loud: “When I have time, I listen to music.”

blocks.md:
To say **“It has been [duration] since I did [action]”**, use:

**[Verb-(으)ㄴ] 지 + [Time] + 됐어요**

한국에 **온 지** 일 년 **됐어요**. / It’s been a year since I came to Korea.
한국어를 **배운 지** 세 달 **됐어요**. / It’s been three months since I started learning Korean.

items.ch: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.
items.tip: It’s been a year since I came to Korea.

items.ch: 한국어를 배운 지 세 달 됐어요.
items.tip: It’s been three months since I learned Korean.
It’s been a long time since I saw my friend.

blocks.q: “한국에 온 ___ 일 년 됐어요.” Which particle completes “since doing”?
blocks.why: The elapsed time pattern is **-(으)ㄴ 지 [time] 됐어요**.

blocks.sentence: 밥을 먹[은 지] 세 시간 됐어요.
blocks.meaning: It has been three hours since I ate.
blocks.why: 먹다 has a consonant 받침 (ㄱ), so it takes -은 지 → **먹은 지**.

blocks.meaning: It has been a long time since I met my friend.
blocks.why: 만나다 ends in vowel ㅏ, so it takes -ㄴ 지 → **만난 지**.

blocks.wrong: 한국어를 배우는 지 삼 개월 됐어요.
answers: 한국어를 배운 지 삼 개월 됐어요
한국어를 배운 지 삼 개월 됐어요.
blocks.hint: The elapsed time pattern takes -(으)ㄴ 지, so 배우다 becomes 배운 지.
blocks.why: Elapsed time requires **-(으)ㄴ 지** → 배운 지.

blocks.q: Write it yourself: **“It has been one year since I came to Korea.”**  (one year = 일 년, to come = 오다)
answers: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요
blocks.hint: Use 오다 + -ㄴ 지 (온 지), followed by 일 년 됐어요.
blocks.why: 한국에 온 지 일 년 됐어요.

blocks.say: 한국어를 배운 지 세 달 됐어요.
blocks.rom: han-gug-eo-reul bae-un ji se dal dwaess-eo-yo
blocks.q: Say it out loud: “It has been three months since I started learning Korean.”

title.ko: 4강. 시간 표현 네 가지의 꼴 만들기
title.en: Lesson 4. Shaping the Four Time Expressions

blocks.h: Batchim Rules Across the 4 Time Patterns
blocks.md:
Let’s look at how the 4 time connectors attach to verb stems:

1. **-기 전에 (Before):** Stems never change! Attach directly: 먹기 전에, 가기 전에.
2. **-(으)ㄴ 후에 (After):** 받침 있음 → **-은 후에**, 받침 없음 → **-ㄴ 후에**.
3. **-(으)ㄹ 때 (When):** 받침 있음 → **-을 때**, 받침 없음 → **-ㄹ 때**.
4. **-(으)ㄴ 지 (Elapsed time):** 받침 있음 → **-은 지**, 받침 없음 → **-ㄴ 지**.
Look at **만들다** (ㄹ stem)! Before ㄴ, the ㄹ drops out: **만든 후에**, **만든 지**. But with -(으)ㄹ 때, the existing ㄹ merges directly: **만들 때** (not 만들을 때)!

items.tip: I wash hands before eating. (먹다 + 기 전에)
Let’s meet after class ends. (끝나다 + ㄴ 후에)
When I have time, I exercise. (있다 + 을 때)

blocks.q: Which form correctly attaches -(으)ㄹ 때 to ‘만나다’ (to meet)?
blocks.why: 만나다 has no final consonant (받침), so it attaches -ㄹ 때 to become **만날 때**.

blocks.q: How does ‘만들다’ (to make) attach to -(으)ㄴ 후에?
blocks.why: Verbs ending in ㄹ drop the ㄹ before ㄴ, resulting in **만든 후에**.

blocks.q: Match each verb and connector to its correct form.

blocks.meaning: Before going out, I check the weather.
blocks.why: The pattern for 'before doing' is **-기 전에**.

blocks.q: Attach -(으)ㄴ 후에 to 먹다 (to eat): 「밥을 ___ 커피를 마셔요.」
blocks.why: 먹다 has a final consonant (ㄱ), so it attaches -은 후에 → **먹은 후에**.

blocks.say: 밥을 먹은 후에 이를 닦고, 자기 전에 책을 읽어요.
blocks.rom: bab-eul meog-eun hu-e i-reul dakk-go, ja-gi jeon-e chaeg-eul ilg-eo-yo
blocks.q: Read out loud connecting the two time patterns naturally.
